frequency_question: How often do complex Western-origin precision missile systems successfully transition to domestic co-production or manufacture in a recipient allied nation within two years of major escalation?
membership_rule: Includes instances where a state at war attempts to establish domestic licensed production of foreign precision-guided munitions (cruise missiles, air defense systems, precision artillery) with allied technical transfer. Excludes simple ammunition or non-guided artillery transfers.

cases.name: Ukraine domestic production of Stugna-P and Neptune (indigenous, not foreign cruise)
Taiwan domestic production of Hsiung Feng missiles with US technical assistance heritage
South Korea domestic licensed production of US precision munitions
Pakistan domestic production of Al-Khalid/Babur with foreign component assistance
Ukraine joint-venture attempts with Western defense contractors post-2022 (general air defense/armor)

coverage_note: 5 named; represents key historical precedents for high-tech defense localization under pressure
known_gaps: Classified or highly proprietary current joint ventures between Western defense primes and Eastern European nations are partially obscured.
skeleton: 5 documented major historical instances of advanced missile technology domestic co-production initiatives under wartime or high-threat duress since 1994
multiplier: 4 hits out of 5 comparable historical precedents of high-tech defense transfers successfully establishing domestic lines within the window
validity_reason: Defense industrial base cooperation models remain stable over multi-year geopolitical cycles.
